We undertook a statistical investigation into tidal features surrounding early-type galaxies of massive proportions, utilizing data from the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program. Our analysis revealed that roughly 28 percent of 2649 galaxies, selected due to their mass greater than $10^{11}M_{\odot}$ and within a redshift range of 0.05-0.15, exhibited distinct tidal features exceeding one percent flux fraction. Observations indicated an exponential decline in the number of galaxies as tidal features became more pronounced. Additionally, within our defined stellar mass scope, we observed tidal features exceeding one percent flux fraction on more than double the number of galaxies when compared to those of lower masses. A comprehensive study of tidal features in early-type galaxies of lighter masses revealed a similar behavior. Our findings are consistent with fewer large tidal features on more massive galaxies due to their increased resistance to mergers. Moreover, we estimated that the merger rates of massive early-type galaxies with respect to other massive galaxies of similar mass are approximately two orders of magnitude lower than their counterparts with lower masses, although they possess larger galaxies of similar masses.

This paper is a component of a research series focusing on the Azimuthally Symmetric Theory of Gravitation (ASTG), a theoretical framework derived from the established equation by Laplace and Poisson. Our findings indicate that, under specific conditions dependent on the object's spin, the ASTG can generate repulsive gravitational fields in the polar regions of massive objects, thereby shedding new light on the phenomenon of outflows as a manifestation of repulsive gravity. This process is an integral component of star formation and has been the subject of extensive debate regarding its origins. This paper departs from our initial study, which described bipolar outflows using the concept of force repulsion with no associated mass loss, by including, in this study, the impact of gravitation on the surrounding material. We conducted two experiments, labeled as replication 1 and replication 2, which involved the simulation of molecular cloud collapse and the evolution of dense cores using the ASTG and GR, respectively. Our experiments showed that, under certain circumstances, the ASTG generates a region of repulsive gravity near the central star but cannot accurately simulate the observed effects of mass loss associated with bipolar outflows observed in star formation. However, when the flow rate is low, as in the case of a fast-moving stream through a region of repulsive gravity, the ASTG can simulate a slight increase in the flow rate.

We have gathered a vast dataset of observations during and following fast radio bursts, making it the largest compilation to date. Our research incorporates a combination of observations, consisting of those made simultaneously or soon after, along with archival survey data which has been extensively analyzed. We've observed FRB 180924, FRB 190102, and FRB 190508 in real-time using the Very Large Array, while deep surveys within the Optical Counter-Part Counter-Explosions Project have provided significant insights into FRB 200117, FRB 200302A, and FRB 200730A. Additionally, archival data from the Zwicky Transient Facility has enabled us to study FRB 20181107A, FRB 20181119A, and FRB 20201147A under a new light. By combining the optical and radio wave trajectories of these FRBs, our findings set new limits on the optical and X-ray emission from these enigmatic events. Analyzing the optical and X-ray emission from magnetic shocks caused by the FRB 20141105A burst led us to conclude that such a shock would not prevent the FRB from persisting. Our research indicates that FRB 20141105A did not have a bright X-ray continuum about 12.5 years prior to the FRB, suggesting that FRB 20141105A may not be the first in a burst sequence that may be powered by a compact object with a strong magnetic field

The combination of chirped pulse amplification and nonlinear optical materials has been the foundation for significant breakthroughs in numerous industries, including semiconductors, communications, biology, defense, and national security. In these fields, researchers have obtained information such as crystallographic structures, atomic compositions, and cellular dynamics using XPBD, SPM, and STED techniques. However, conformal simulations remain an unsolved challenge in many cases due to the complex interactions in laser-material interactions, and only a few successful examples have been reported. In this paper, we present a novel pan-physical modeling approach to optimize high-power laser systems that take into account all major factors influencing their performance. The development of a unified, open-source Python library, called HipHure, is also discussed, and it is successfully applied to the design of an industrial-coating Turner laser. Furthermore, the framework is extended to model free-electron lasing, and a structured light field is applied to improve its efficiency by factors of 2 and 3 respectively, and the results are compared to experimental measurements. The framework is now available online at https://github.com/hiphure.

Multimodal language generation capabilities of models like GPT-2 and GPT-3 can be
utilized for producing high-quality text, but it is still difficult for them to
determine what they should be writing about based on the provided context. In
order to address this issue, we suggest employing a specific strategy where
relevant visual information is integrated into the input of these models to aid
in their understanding of the context. We present a new approach called CIG, which
combines existing vision-and-language processing techniques to automatically
extract visual features from external sources and add them to the input of the
language model as controls, thereby guiding its focus for text production.
Experimental results obtained with GPT-2 and GPT-3 demonstrate that our approach
leads to the discovery of novel innovative and creative written outputs on both
conversational and writing tasks. These findings clearly illustrate the
capability of language models to 'look' at visual information when producing text
and how this can be leveraged in various real-world applications to boost their
productivity.

We introduce an upgraded RingCT protocol that supports stealth addresses in conjunction with Delegated Proof of Stake, resulting in Delegated RingCT.
The Delegated RingCT scheme is comprised of an integrated signature and encryption framework, combining a public key encryption protocol and two types of signatures along with linkable ring signatures, alongside non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs.
A comprehensive description of Delegated RingCT, along with security evidence and an implemented prototype, are presented, which we subsequently test through benchmarking analysis.
While Delegated RingCT may not possess the same level of anonymity compared to other RingCT implementations, we propose that its ability to be compatible with DPoS consensus mechanisms provides a reasonable trade-off for enabling more secure and efficient transaction execution.
In practice, Delegated RingCT is shown to significantly reduce the computational requirements and transaction output sizes when compared to other RingCT implementations.

In 2015, CERN introduced "Emittance Scans," a new fast luminosity separation scanning method at the Large Hadron Collider. These scans were consistently carried out during physics production runs, utilizing full-intensity beams at the CMS experiment's interaction point. The emittance scans allowed for the simultaneous measurement of beam properties and an assessment of the impact of dynamics factors, such as kick off offset and horizontal and vertical optics, on beam performance. The tests demonstrated that by minimizing these effects, beam performance could be maximized, resulting in a 10% emittance increase. Recent breakthroughs in artificial intelligence capabilities have created opportunities for machine learning models to significantly contribute to the simulation-based engineering field. These advances have paved the way for data-driven modeling to supplement traditional physical modeling. Initially, data-driven models were viewed as a replacement for physical models, but they are now recognized as a valuable complementary tool that offers unique benefits, including streamlined processes and rapid results. One of the major advantages of data-driven models is their potential to produce accurate outputs with limited or no prior knowledge, due to their ability to automatically detect relevant data characteristics. This article provides an overview of the practical application of cooperative machine learning, with a focus on data-driven modeling. It starts with an examination of the inherent complexities of mechanical engineering models that often consist of multiple interconnected modules and then outlines the key characteristics of cooperative machine learning. Following this, the article discusses the current limitations of using data-driven models in mechanical engineering and presents case studies that highlight the feasibility of cooperative machine learning in this field. Finally, the article identifies areas where further research is required to fully incorporate data-driven modeling into mechanical engineering practices.

This research examines the decay of the $\Upsilon(10753)$ into a $\Upsilon(nS)$
state accompanied by $\pi^+\pi^-$ particles, where $n=1,2,3$. It's assumed
$\Upsilon(10753)$ belongs to a typical bottomonium under the universal potential
model, with a central charge of $-0.65$ between $b$ and $b'$ quarks. Our
findings based on the universal potential model and a quark model show that
experimental verification of the $\Upsilon(10753)$ state can provide crucial
validation for recent findings on the $\Upsilon(5S)$ and $\Upsilon(6S)$ states.
Moreover, our analysis generates predictive decay branching fractions for
comparison with future experimental results.

This paper presents a novel optimization technique called AskewSGD to efficiently train deep neural networks with quantized weights. Initially, we transform the quantized neural network training into a sequence of constrained optimization problems that can be iteratively refined. Our method, AskewSGD, is an efficient first-order stochastic approach designed to solve these optimization problems. AskewSGD combines geometric constraints with a tailored regularizer to converge toward optimal solutions. We derive convergence bounds for AskewSGD under common machine learning assumptions. Our empirical evaluations demonstrate askerss's exceptional performance in training quantized neural networks, often surpassing other state-of-the-art methods under different training settings and data types.

The Continuum Soft Robot project utilizes fully flexible mechanical systems to achieve robots that more closely resemble the anatomy of invertebrate creatures and flexible body parts of vertebrates. To introduce the concepts and challenges of this innovative area in robotics, we will be adopting a control theorist's approach, simplifying the entry into this field by systematically presenting current research and future obstacles through a uniform language and organized structure. The primary hurdles to participating in this area are the vast differences in terminology and perspectives. The proposed framework divides the topics into four categories: the definitions of Continuum Soft Robots, their physical characteristics, the underlying mathematical models, and the control strategies, allowing us to summarize the current state of research and identify areas for future investigation. We will examine the relevant terminology, characterizing the characteristics of Continuum Soft Robots and their fundamental that must be considered in designing their controllers. We will also discuss the dominant approaches to developing continuum robot ground-up models and control strategies, highlighting their strengths and weaknesses.

One form of the realisation involves the determinant being a homomorphism to $\mathbb{R}$. Moreover, the group $G^J_1(\mathbb{R})$ can be identified with a subgroup of ${\rm SL}(4,\mathbb{R})$ via matrix embedding. Another realisation of the Jacobi group involves combining two copies of the ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ group in a manner analogous to its known 2x2 realisation. Verifying facts using structured data can be difficult, necessitating a model's
understanding of both language and symbolic computations. Our research tackles
this challenge by employing program synthesis to build a compositional model of
the world. In the context of multi-step factual assertions, our method trains a
model that recognizes applicable operations on a given table. It then uses this
model to guide the synthesis of a program that verifies the factual statement.
We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach through empirical assessments and
compare it to existing state-of-the-art models.

The state of the art in learned synthetic image generation involves generative adversarial networks. Initial breakthroughs in the field relied on unsupervised approaches, however, current advancements are primarily based on labelled data, leading to increased control, flexibility, and stability in the generated images. Notably, these supervised methods require substantial amounts of annotated data, posing a major challenge. Our proposed framework combines two powerful techniques: adversarial training and representation learning, ultimately contributing to the development of unsupervised high-quality GANs. Our novel mechanism allows for the guidance of GANs by an external latent space, thereby achieving more control when compared to previous approaches. We achieve this by designing conditions specifically tailored for an augmented GAN architecture that expands its latent space, thereby yielding nearly unsupervised results. Our framework exhibits superior performance in both natural and medical image generation tasks, demonstrating the potential for the integration of an latent space to drive GANs towards more efficient and productive training.

To perform Bayesian inference using nested sampling, a specific prior sampling approach must be used to compile a list of samples from accepted prior values. The choice of sampling technique greatly has influence on the efficiency of nested sampling. We introduce and explore a class of algorithms known as "step samplers," which offer great potential in optimizing the nested sampling process. Unlike traditional algorithms, step samplers take full advantage of the information gained during each successful transition. In this research, we evaluate several step samplers within nested sampling scenarios, considering their performance across various distributions. Our investigation is combined with real-world applications from cosmology, astrophysics, and medicine, allowing us to compare the efficiency of different step samplers in practical scenarios where multiple parameters are involved. Overall, our research aims to understand and compare these efficient step samplers in complex Bayesian analyses, while providing valuable insights to guide their practical use.

In fault-tolerant distance labelling, we're tasked with assigning brief descriptions to the points in a network so that knowing any three points' labels allows us to deduce the direct distance between any two of them, excluding the third. Our work proves that any weighted network with a specific layout (or in fact any network with limited separating elements) allows the assignment of brief descriptions with a specific length, that enables the inference of distances in networks with one point removed. These descriptions are further adapted to track the number of shortest paths, while providing bounds on label and counting oracle sizes.

In this theoretical study, we explore two-particle correlation functions in a Bose-Hubbard model subject to external driving and dissipation, specifically at the quantum phase transition where excitations are prominent. Using the Keldysh perturbation method, we calculated frequency-dependent two-particle self-energy terms and time-evolutionary two-particle correlation functions, enabling us to analyze non-stationary behavior in a Bose-Hubbard model with dissipation. Our findings indicate that, despite increasing dissipation, we can observe two-particle correlation functions that are similar to those of the driven model, both in time and frequency domains. Additionally, our model's response to excitations near the quantum phase transition reveals a significant impact of tunneling strength on the spectral weight in two-particle correlation functions, a phenomenon that is not observable in the driven, dissipationless model.

For a given second-order linear elliptic equation with coefficients $A$, $\mathbf{b}$ and a parameter $\lambda$, defined within a bounded $\mathbb{R}^2$ domain $\Omega$ and satisfying specific smoothness and boundedness conditions, we establish existence and uniqueness of the weak solution in $W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$ for the Dirichlet problem, where $2<p<\infty$, assuming that the equation also includes source and flux terms. Similar results are obtained for the corresponding dual problem under analogous conditions.

To ensure that medical imaging models produce accurate predictions, it is crucial to implement out-of-distribution detection capabilities. There are doubts whether traditional deep neural network-based methods are effective in identifying shifts in data distributions. In contrast, Bayesian models are well-equipped to recognize unknown environments due to their inherent uncertainty handling mechanism. Nevertheless, the uncertainty measures provided by Bayesian models can be influenced by various sources of uncertainty that are not predictive. To tackle this challenge, we incorporate Gaussian Processes Layers, which can separate uncertainty stemming from data usage from that which is intrinsic to the data itself, into a medical imaging convolutional neural network. Our model is then utilized for out-of-distribution detection in various datasets. The results indicate that Gaussian Processes Layers produce accurate detections by effectively distinguishing between known and unknown environments. Furthermore, the model's ability to extract relevant uncertainty signals was also validated through an ablation study.

The ideal gas law applies to gases where components move freely and randomly, leading to a defined temperature. In contrast, particles in a confined, isolated environment adhere to this law only when they exhibit random motion. For systems of isolated particles or those within a sealed box, the temperature is a relevant and useful concept. However, for particles or systems within an open environment, the term "temperature" is less useful and often replaced by "chemical potential." These definitions apply to physical systems through various models. Our research extends this to quantum systems with multiple particles by describing it mathematically. Through a simulation based on the Bose-Hubbard model, our prediction is that any isolated system will develop a condensate of particles when it reaches a maximum possible temperature, even without any potential for attraction between particles. Our results also demonstrate the development of a condensate in an isolated system through heat exchange between different parts of the system. Our research shows that an isolated system cannot maintain a condensate of particles if it has a connection to its environment, unless it reaches its maximum possible temperature. Additionally, our results validate that different definitions of temperature and chemical potential align when a system of particles is in a state of random motion. Our research was conducted using an artificial system consisting of two separate particles, driven by a laser to simulate random motion, providing insight into experiments that study the behavior of particles.

The article explores the convex solution $u$ of the Monge--Amp\`ere equation in an open convex domain with a nonnegative, bounded right-hand side, along with specific boundary data. A key finding relates Alexandrov's maximum principle, specifically its equivalence to H\"older continuity, for convex functions with zero boundary data. Furthermore, it has been proven that convex $\alpha$-H\"older continuous functions fall into $W^{1,p}$ for $p<1/(1{-}\alpha)$. Utilizing these outcomes, the article establishes the H\"older continuity of the convex function $u$, with sharp bounds derived through a specific calculation, even in the case of a right-hand function that is simply bounded.

Counting the recurrence of periodic events allows us to measure time. Historically, developing stable and accurate timekeeping devices was a significant undertaking. We will instead examine a different class of timekeeping devices, based on unstable optical systems, where the concept of recurrence needs to be redefined. A theoretical framework has been developed for these devices by analytically studying the behavior of two oscillating systems in phase space. A statistical model has been created that allows for time estimation by analyzing the patterns of these systems over long periods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach with two hypothetical examples and discuss its practical implications. This research opens up a new avenue for investigating time's fundamental properties using both traditional and optical systems.

This research centers on Software Defined Networks (SDN) to address the challenges of traffic engineering, fault prevention, and service delivery within reliability and energy constraints. Utilizing Fog computing, we focus on optimizing distributed traffic flows to achieve real-time service delivery, effective failure recovery, and fault-awareness in the context of Service Function Chains (SFCs). To address these issues, we developed an FRFP architecture and two algorithms: the Optimal Fog-Supported Energy-Aware SFC routing algorithm (OFES-F) and the near-optimal, real-time Fog-Supported Failure-aware SFC routing algorithm (RTFF-F). By comparing the proposed solutions with current frameworks, we demonstrated that our approaches lead to substantial improvements in terms of energy efficiency, network reliability, and latency reduction.

Metric learning's pair-wise loss technique is centered around optimizing an embedding that maximizes similarity between images within the same class, minimizing distance between images in distinct classes. Various forms of pair-wise loss strategies have been proposed. To consolidate this diverse set of loss functions, we've isolated specific aspects that dictate how these functions manipulate the positioning of feature pairs. Breaking down pair-wise gradient updates this way enables us to 1) identify commonalities among different loss functions, 2) develop a more unified understanding of how they work, and 3) create a new loss function, referred to as Pairwise-Surgery loss, that incorporates the insights from our analysis. Our research results reveal that the proposed loss functions produce comparable results with the state-of-the-art on the standard datasets (CUB-200-2011, Stanford Cars, Stanford Planes).

In this context, we explore certain classes of holographic tensor networks, which can efficiently simulate various systems using the principle of minimization, serve as quantum codes to prevent information loss, and accurately describe phenomena exhibiting power-law behaviors. A key finding reveals that networks comprising a single type of tensor and possessing erasure correction capabilities can't simultaneously possess certain desirable traits - those that facilitate the efficient calculation of physical properties through a local process and those necessary for an accurate representation of power-law behaviors in data. This contradiction motivates the creation of network guidelines that utilize diverse types of tensors, allowing these networks to successfully capture the characteristics of power-law behaviors while adhering to the principle of efficient calculation. A concrete example of such a network has also been developed - one that resembles the holographic HaPPY pentagon code under an assumption that can simplify the principle of minimization. This new variation of the HaPPY code has the potential to effectively simulate quantum systems with a decreasing correlation radius.

Our study of magnetized radio filaments at the center of the galaxy utilizes MeerKAT data by examining the distances between groups of these filaments. Despite limited data and complex background noise, we managed to detect two notable cluster types: groups of 2-3 and groups of 4 filaments, showing characteristic spacings of approximately 300-400 and 800 parsecs respectively. Using a statistical analysis model, we compared these findings with the expected distribution if filament spacing followed a random process generated by the galaxy's magnetic field structure. While the data does not offer conclusive evidence, it suggests that the observed spacings could be the result of interaction between magnetic strands, indicating a time scale of approximately 50,000-200,000 years in the development of these filament clusters. This is in line with the time it takes for star-forming gas to deplete in the galactic center region. Moreover, the large spacings observed between filament groups may be influenced by their orientation, following primarily due to their proximity to the Galactic Plane, leading to the partial shadowing effect of adjacent filaments.

A proposed paper suggests a new method of distributed leader-follower conservation voltage reduction across unmanaged low-voltage distribution networks. The method requires the immediate substation transformer to manage its own load as well as downstream loads by optimizing voltage levels through smart management. Leveraging existing infrastructure, this approach can increase renewable energy generation efficiency, reduce energy consumption, and decrease power losses without altering the primary circuit. The method works by an optimized primary substation automatically calculating optimal tap positions to adjust voltage levels, while secondary smart devices manage their own power flow and consume minimum energy while maintaining network voltage levels. The method effectively addresses the bottleneck limiting primary and secondary optimization and enables efficient renewal of low-voltage distribution networks. The method's performance has been tested using real-world data and compared with conventional conservation voltage reduction techniques.

We investigate non-stochastic bandits and experts in a delayed context, where delays are contingent upon both time and arm choice. While delayed settings with time-dependent delays have been thoroughly studied, considering arm-dependent delays in non-stochastic scenarios remains novel. In this paper, we address this gap by first developing a dynamic priority schedule, which achieves an optimal $\Omega(\sqrt{T})$ regret in the large arm variety scenario for $N$ experts and $K$ arms with $K \leq N$. Notably, this method enables us to solve an open problem stated by Gutmann et al. for the special case of $K=1$, yielding a regret lower bound under a specific condition and confirming the optimality of a previously proposed heuristic by Cao et al. when delays are time-dependent. Furthermore, we extend our approach to the multiple experts setting with $N$ experts and $K$ arms, which is left unsolved in its current form by Gutmann et al. Next, we explore a more complex scenario in which time and arm dependency of delays are both non-constant and vary infinitely, which is reduced to a more tractable problem by sampling a delay at a finite rate. We then derive a regret lower bound for this reduced problem and prove that our previously designed algorithm is optimal, yielding a regret of $\Omega(T^{3/4})$ for $N$ experts and $K$ arms. This result is an improvement over known regret bounds for time-dependent delay settings

Current text-generation algorithms in dialogue can be flawed. Specifically, optimizing task success using reinforcement learning alone often leads to low lexical diversity in task-oriented settings. The proposed reason is a lack of fundamental understanding of text-generation objectives and how they impact the learning process during model training. A novel theoretical framework has been developed for modeling the text-generation process in a cognitive manner. Based on this framework, a simple reward mechanism is introduced that mimics the effect of intrinsic motivation in psychology. The effectiveness of this new learning paradigm has been tested in both task-oriented and multi-turn domains for generating human-like dialogue. The proposed approach is compatible with existing baselines and does not require additional features or components. The results show that this algorithm can produce text similar to that written by humans without requiring human-labeled examples. The proposed framework has also provided valuable insights into the effect of specific optimization parameters on the learning process and the quality of generated text.

Following Quantum Chromodynamics' 1972 formulation, a breakthrough in its regularization came when Kenneth Wilson applied it to Euclidean lattices. This opened doors for in-depth numerical analyses of QCD's non-perturbative features, exemplified in the initial studies by Michael Creutz. Subsequently, investigations into the QCD phase diagram and the thermodynamics of hot, dense strong-interaction matter gained significant momentum. In this concise review, some key outcomes from over four decades of lattice QCD research on QCD thermodynamics are compiled.

A type of Gaussian process regression that accounts for the variability in data points, called heteroscedastic Gaussian process regression, is utilized to establish a statistical model for predicting the complex loads experienced by offshore wind turbines, thereby informing the estimation of structural loads for these turbines. Since evaluating these loads through physical testing and experimental simulations is costly in terms of time and resources, a new approach to statistical modeling, referred to as probabilistic surrogate modeling, is applied using a sequence of Gaussian processes that progressively account for the increasing uncertainties in the data sets. This model is developed by integrating and conditioning successive Gaussian processes, thereby incorporating the varying levels of noise within the data sets, and this approach has the added advantage of enabling the creation of a probabilistic model from uncertain computational data. Furthermore, a method for efficiently estimating the noise within Gaussian processes, based on the statistical analysis of residuals, is developed and this approach is applied to the analysis of data obtained from offshore wind-turbine experiments.

Turkey is prone to seismic activities with varying intensity earthquakes occurring frequently, emphasizing the necessity for swift and effective crisis information dissemination. Social media can provide valuable insights into public perception, beneficial for crisis communication and management. This research focuses on analyzing Twitter posts related to the 2020 Izmir earthquake, aiming to leverage these insights to infer real-time public opinions. By combining data mining and natural language processing techniques, we examine public sentiment and topic discussions following the earthquake. Our approach utilized LDA for topic modeling and BERT for sentiment analysis. Results show users shared supportive messages and engaged with relief efforts, expressing their desire to have their concerns heard by authorities. The implemented methodology demonstrated success in identifying earthquake-related tweets, accurately capturing topic transitions and initially fluctuating sentiment which later turned negative due to the lack of efficient crisis communication and inadequate assistance provided by the government. This research showcases a viable framework for analyzing and understanding public sentiment and discussions on social media during crises.

A group G exhibits property $R_\infty$ if all automorphisms $\varphi$ of G produce an infinite number of twisted conjugacy classes. In such cases, we determine which nilpotent quotients of generalized solvable Baumslag-Solitar groups possess the $R_\infty$ property.

A new technique is developed to process time-sensitive data from ultra-fast experiments using an approach based on optimization in a pathway framework. This technique is employed to break down complex events into their fundamental components, such as the occurrence of multiple concurrent processes. It also relies on the analysis of molecular dynamics simulations to determine a suitable coordinate system for the pathway, which in turn is supported by the examination of molecular events across different states. To address issues of data noise, the technique includes a model that incorporates data errors and incorporates data points that best align with the pathway. This technique is validated through its application in the re reduction of trans-1,3,3-diphenylpropane and the analysis of its own ability to accurately describe the reaction and account for relevant molecular vibrations is discussed.

This paper presents SceNDD: a novel naturalistic driving dataset derived from
instrumented vehicle data collected in downtown Indianapolis over the course
of 68 driving sessions with various drivers. Each session lasted approximately
20 to 40 minutes. Our primary aim in creating this dataset is to supply the
research community with realistic driving scenarios encompassing diverse
trajectories and driving behaviors. SceNDD features a comprehensive set of data,
including the ego-vehicle's waypoints, velocity, and yaw angle, as well as
similar metrics for non-ego actors. Additionally, we allow users to customize
existing scenarios by introducing additional elements, such as actors, sensors,
lanes, roads, and obstacles. A Joint Probabilistic Data Association tracker was
utilized to identify non-ego vehicles. We present some preliminary outcomes of
the dataset, along with potential applications, and anticipate the complete
release of SceNDD in early 2023.

A novel approach to conformal field theory in two dimensions is offered by reflection and interface theories. These are essentially cutting-edge developments in boundary and interface conformal field theory. As a result, researchers are still working on fully developing this concept. To achieve this, a new physical system, reflected entropy, is introduced. It represents the entropy of two entangled states after reflecting it against the vacuum. Reflected entropy has a dual equivalent in holographic theory as a specific entanglement entropy calculation. It has been proven that reflected entropy has all the properties required for it to be a good conformal block. Moreover, researchers have successfully computed reflected entropies for a number of key states in the radial symmetric two-dimensional black hole case, including primary fields, twist operators, and degenerate states. These computations have provided new insights into fundamental problems, such as the strong subadditivity of entropy and a specific entropy inequality.

Research on Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS)-assisted Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) systems has intensified due to their potential for controlling the communication environment effectively. Nonetheless, the precision of channel estimation in such systems is significantly compromised by the increased risk of underestimating training sequences caused by additional processing delays within the RIS. To address this challenge, we introduce Enhanced Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) models for assisted OFDM systems characterized by insufficient cyclic prefix lengths, hardware imperfections, and varying sizes of training sequences. Our experimental findings reveal that the novel models significantly mitigate the adverse effects of CP shortages, hardware noise, and training sequence lengths on channel estimation accuracy. Moreover, their performance is comparable to that of Model-Aware Channel Estimation, a more sophisticated method that takes into account the influence of neural network models.

We are investigating a type of equality related to the work exerted on a system being observed with unqualified measurement methods. Unlike projective measurements, which are based on the Schrödinger equation, unqualified measurements don't necessarily have this basis. The system we're studying is an open one, connected to a heat bath, and we're exploring work done through energy exchanges based on a single energy observation. We're deriving a work equality that's tailored to this specific scenario and valid under all conditions, despite the work equality for full projective measurements not holding true in all circumstances. Additionally, we're studying a type of equality related to work done in conjunction with this single energy observation and finding it holds under all conditions as well. We're also studying if this single energy observation work equality holds when considering multiple observations being made consecutively and finding it holds true as well. We're also considering if this single energy observation work equality holds when considering a type of therapy and finding it does hold true as well. We're also considering the two-way work equality and finding it does not hold true in all circumstances when considering work done through multiple observations being made consecutively. However, we're also considering a type of therapy and finding the two-way work equality does hold true as well.

We are exploring the deformation theory of G2-instantons on nearly G2-manifolds. A one-to-one connection exists between nearly parallel G2 structures and real Killing spinors, enabling the deformation theory to be formulated through the use of spinors and Dirac operators. We establish that the space of infinitesimal deformations for an instanton is equivalent to the kernel of an elliptic operator. With this theory, we prove that abelian instantons exhibit rigidity, and relate the deformation theory of Hopf instantons to the fundamental group of the Hopf 7-sphere.

The global spread of the 2019 COVID-19 pandemic caused by SARS-CoV-2 has resulted in widespread losses and socio-economic disruption, with the rapid proliferation of the virus having far-reaching effects worldwide. As part of the effort to combat this crisis, contact tracing technology, known for its success in other outbreaks, has been widely adopted.  However, this technology poses significant concerns regarding user data security, as it entails data collection and analysis that can potentially reveal an individual's identity, location, and behavior. The implications of this are especially dire when considering large-scale government surveillance in countries with restrictive policies.  Despite national laws and guidelines intended to standardize data management, practices vary significantly in countries with different systems, further complicating assessment and comparison of contact tracing apps.  This work aims to address these concerns by developing a security protocol for contact tracing apps that utilizes the Coronav′irus-SUS protocol as a reference, specifically minimizing the data required for contact tracing operations.  Furthermore, a detailed analysis will be conducted to evaluate the security and privacy features of national apps based on this standard, with a specific comparison of the Brazilian app, Saúde, in relation to protocols not involving the Coronav′irus-SUS standard.

The central nervous system's underlying physiological processes that drive conscious experiences and mental states are complex and multifaceted. For the most part, these dynamics have been studied from a classical perspective, yet recent advances have made it possible to evaluate their relevance to quantum mechanical models. This book explores the implications of incorporating quantum effects into biological and psychological phenomena, while also providing a framework for understanding the interplay between quantum and classical models. A key aspect of this research involves identifying the quantum resources required to model a system. This field of study, known as quantum resource theory, allows us to systematically evaluate the significance of quantum properties like entanglement and nonlocality in complex data patterns and cognitive processes.

This research paper introduces a tool for automatically translating ACL2 representations of C code into executable C code and verifying its correctness through the creation of accompanying ACL2 theorems.

A cluster of young compact asteroids connected to 39991 Iochroma undergoes a dynamics analysis in this study. Our findings show the Iochroma family's location within two adjacent three-body resonance zones - specifically 3J-1M-3 and 5J 3S-2. This paper establishes the precise positioning of these resonances as well as their demarcation boundary, providing orbital elements approximations that can inform future Iochroma family dynamics research. Moreover, the study identifies a previously unrecognized member of this family, asteroid 2016 UT3.

Building upon Ramanujan's well-known formula for odd zeta values, we establish a related expression using the Hurwitz zeta function. We introduce a novel integral kernel that relates to the Hurwitz zeta function and serves as an extension of the integral kernel linked to Ramanujan's identity. Additionally, we deduce various infinite families of identities comparable to Ramanujan's formula.

We calculate rational T-equivariant elliptic cohomology of complex projective spaces derived from finite dimensional T-representations V. This is accomplished by establishing that the T-equivariant elliptic cohomology theory constructed in Gre05, and the T^2-equivariant theory constructed in Bar22, share a key decomposition. This key decomposition facilitates reducing the T-equivariant cohomology computation to T^2-equivariant cohomology of complex spheres, whose computation is already available from Bar22.

Recent uses of machine learning in algebraic geometry and physics are explored,  
revealing how problems in this field can be easily translated into tensor mapping,  
a concept suitable for supervised learning, as well as offering a chance to use unsupervised  
methods to analyze geometrical data. A primary aspect of this project involves understanding  
how to use geometry within machine learning, as well as how artificial intelligence can be applied  
to advance mathematical research. This discussion is featured as a chapter within the book,  
Machine learning and Algebraic Geometry, edited by A. Kasprzyk.

This paper provides a comprehensive, next-to-leading-order examination of the angular distributions in $J/\psi$ production through $e^{+}e^{-} \to J/\psi + \eta_c, \chi_{cJ}$ ($J=0,1,2$) with the PS-MNR model. The model successfully accounts for nonsingular components and provides a detailed, next-to-leading-order description of experimental results. Utilizing a combined fit of $J/\psi + \eta_c$ and $J/\psi + \chi_{c0}$ angular distributions, we estimate the magnitude of color octet components in $J/\psi + \eta_c$ production to be $\xi_{8}^{(1)} < 0.55$ at 95% confidence level. The model also predicts that $J/\psi + \chi_{c1}$ and $J/\psi + \chi_{c2}$ distributions will have smaller, non-singlet contributions. The combination of experimental data on $J/\psi + \eta_c, J/\psi + \chi_{c0}$ and predicted $J/\psi + \chi_{c1}$, $J/\psi + \chi_{c2}$ angular distributions indicates the nonsinglet PS-MMR model provides a satisfactory description of experimental findings.

Our online survey with 235 Signal users revealed that users can be divided into two categories: those who need additional protection or have complex connections with others, and those who are protected by default due to their limited social network. Upon deconstructing the survey responses, we found that users who aren't required to use PINs lack understanding of how they work, while users who do use PINs have a more intuitive knowledge of the process. The study further showed that users who have more connections online are more likely to be required to use PINs in the future, indicating that Signal's protection rules can automatically apply to users based on their social connections.

This technical note details the development of Gaussian quadrature rules designed to efficiently and precisely evaluate the integrals of products involving the solar irradiance function, as defined by ASTM standards, and user-defined smooth functions. The method's ability to produce accurate results with minimal evaluations is particularly beneficial due to the solar irradiance function's non-smooth, highly oscillatory nature. The accompanying Julia software facilitates the computation of solar-weighted quadrature rules across varying bandwidths or point counts. The described technique is anticipated to significantly aid solar-energy computations, where the user-defined function may involve complex and time-consuming calculations such as absorbance derived from solving Maxwell's equations.

The curvature formed by the Hessian matrix or its generalized Gauss-Newton approximation holds significant value in developing training algorithms for deep networks. However, current methods based on automatic differentiation and Kronecker-factored block diagonal approximations disregard noise in mini-batch datasets. Our new model, ViViT, capitalizes on a low-rank structure within the generalized Gauss-Newton approximation without introducing additional simplifications, thereby allowing for the maintenance of complex layer structures and efficient computation of rich network models. Through comprehensive testing on various tasks, including computer vision and NLP, it has been found that ViViT produces accurate predictions and effective optimization performance by accurately modeling the curvature of multi-layer networks.

Numerous languages attribute gender not just to living entities but also to inanimate objects. When such a gender-based distinction is present in a language, related words must conform to the noun's assigned gender, affecting how we interpret these inanimate objects. As inanimate objects sharing the same gender draw closer together in word representations, we observe this distinct categorization in these languages. However, conventional neural models for inductive word representations do not accurately capture this distinction. To rectify this, we suggest an updated set of word embeddings that incorporates grammatical gender characteristics. We examine the various Grammatical Gender Encoding Techniques that assign gender to inanimate objects and evaluate several methods to determine which one is most effective. Our research demonstrates the importance of incorporating grammatical gender characteristics into inductive word representations, especially in languages expressing gender through inanimate objects. We create an extended dataset, CoGGender, for benchmarking Grammatical Gender Encoding Techniques in more than 10 languages. CoGGender allows researchers to assess the success of these techniques in achieving improved representation of inanimate objects that assign grammatical gender.

We categorize and understand a certain aspect of attractiveness in groups that use arithmetic, and derive statements indicating a dual nature related to their stable components, characteristics, and associated algebraic structures. To accomplish this, we study the movement patterns over the characteristics of the embedded form of these groups, specifically proving them inflexible and establishing a correlation with their stable properties, which is consistent with a long-standing theory proposed by Borel. This line of reasoning is based on a framework combining ideas from representation theory, geometric measurements, and the theory of characteristics developed by Serre.

Estimating an object's pose is a crucial aspect of most visual pipelines in robots and 3D vision as a whole. This study tackles the challenge of accurately positioning new objects with no prior knowledge. This method builds on previous work by removing the necessity for object-pose-labelled data or category-specific 3D models during both training and inference. Our core idea is to utilize a different point cloud compared to the one used for feature extraction. By doing so, the pose of the object in the new point cloud can be determined by maximizing their similarity while aligning the two clouds. Experiments on a robot and 3D mesh rendering show our method to be versatile and reliable, performing on par with existing techniques in many scenarios. One key benefit is that it allows for the estimation of object poses in very tight spaces. Our proposed framework is well-suited for automation as it requires almost no human intervention. This research is further detailed in the link below:

https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.01494

Predicting short-term traffic is a widely researched area within intelligent transportation systems. However, existing forecasting systems face significant limitations due to their reliance on real-time data. The 2022 Traffic4cast challenge at NeurIPS addressed this issue by using publicly available sparse data. Our team submitted a solution to the expanded challenge of predicting estimated time of arrival. Our method involves extracting multiple feature sets - node flow characteristics, segment-based attributes, and similarity-based properties, which we used to train a model based on decision trees with gradient boosting. Our results demonstrate exceptional predictive capabilities across three cities - London, Madrid, and Melbourne - and even surpass some graph neural network-based approaches in estimating travel times. Our source code is available at https://github.com/c-lyu/Traffic4Cast2022-TSE.

This study presents VACA, a new family of variational graph autoencoders developed specifically for causal inference and counterfoudral analysis. By integrating graph-based variational autoencoders with key causal concepts such as structural causal models, counterfactuals and interventions, we create a versatile model that enables prediction of key causal variables: counterfactual outcomes, interventional missing data and treat-the-control estimates. We establish a general framework for training these models on observational data, which can then be extended to manipulate parameters in scenarios involving causal graphs with unknown network structure. We demonstrate the effectiveness of VACA through simulations on various generative models and a real-world application in pre-intervention analysis of asthma treatment for children.

State-of-the-art radio interferometers such as the LOw Frequency ARray (LOFAR) are now capable of producing massive data at speeds of hundreds of gigabits to terabits per second. This significant data rate complicates radio data analysis and necessitates costly computation. Although top-tier computing facilities are accessible for 24/7 processing, decentralized data processing using edge Graphical Processing Units (GPUs) and System on a Chip (SoC) offers an alternative solution. Our team successfully deployed a demonstration setup for the edge data processing concept at the Irish LOFAR site. In this research, we showcase the effectiveness of edge data processing and its capabilities, and discuss its importance for the future of radio astronomy.

In recent years, advancements in machine learning and artificial intelligence have driven significant growth in photonics research, leading to cutting-edge photonic systems including traditional waveguides, nanoantennas, and metasurfaces. The innovative concept of metascale optics, which governs light interaction with matter, is now being revamped with AI and machine learning. This review article provides an overview of cutting-edge AI-powered metascale optics, starting with basic machine learning-based systems that learn light interaction rules and evolve into data-driven systems for optimal photonic device design. We also explore current photonic device applications, such as highly-sensitive sensors for biological detection, advanced photonic biosensors, and virtually-indexed metasurface devices for both conventional and novel applications like biomedical technology, to highlight the potential of intelligent metascale optics for future photonic device research and development.

The high-risk, high-reward nature of filmmaking means predicting which movies will be profitable at the box office has become a daunting task. In an effort to minimize financial losses, major film producers and studios continually seek a more reliable method for estimating movie revenue before making an investment. Researchers from the film industry have faced this challenge by attempting to develop their own predictive models, but the relatively small size of traditional movie datasets has hindered significant breakthroughs in this area. In an attempt to fill this gap, our team has assembled a substantially larger, more comprehensive movie dataset that spans over a decade, distinguishing us from prior initiatives. This comprehensive dataset allows us to perform more accurate and detailed analysis, including an exploration of how movie characteristics like cast size, runtime, and rating can influence box office revenue, and identify the most critical factors contributing to higher grossing films. By retaining up-to-date attributes and an extensive dataset spanning over a decade, our dataset is positioned to facilitate future research on movie profitability, making it an invaluable resource for researchers and filmmakers alike.

This study examines the effect of secondary frequency control on voltage oscillations. We show that beyond its role in maintaining grid frequency stability, its rapid response has a profound impact on voltage dynamics, particularly during disturbances. We investigated how the LC filter in power electronics-based converters affects the complex behavior of power electronics under secondary frequency control, using phase-plane analysis to identify and visualize patterns in the filter's behavior and their influence on stability. Our results, backed by numerical simulations, demonstrate the difference in behavior between primary and secondary frequency control and highlight the potential risks of using secondary frequency control alone in converter-based systems.

Cyber Physical Systems are greatly benefiting from the concept of systems of systems. This is particularly true, as the emerging CPS of of Systems paradigm is providing a foundational framework for integrating and blending together independent CPS systems to form a unified, cohesive entity. The integration of these systems has proven challenging due to disparate technological and tactical aspects, requiring collaboration models, and varying security measures. Conversely, the Systems of Systems approach empowers diverse CPS to work together in unison, enhancing their functionality and complexity through cooperative action. It's through this cooperative action that a unified, cohesive CPS of of Systems can emerge, achieving goals previously thought unattainable. The Systems of Systems paradigm is seen as a promise, offering a future where diverse systems work in harmony to achieve a unified, cohesive goal. Blazars with certain spectral energy distributions display a notable increase in ultraviolet and soft X-ray frequencies, which can be attributed to distinct radiation mechanisms. By analyzing the polarization patterns of UV and X-ray emissions from these blazars, scientists can gain a deeper understanding of the complex astrophysical environment surrounding blazar jets, allowing for predictions about associated polarization properties. This research employs a novel Monte-Carlo code called MAPPIES to simulate and calculate the polarization characteristics of a hypothetical blazar model that exhibits a break in its spectral energy distribution, which corresponds to a particular radio galaxy, BL Lacz U1556-780. Our findings indicate that, under specific conditions, the polarization angle of X-rays emitted from this blazar may exhibit a change in rotation, reaching a maximum divergence of about twenty degrees from the expected parallel trend with UV polarization angle orientation.

In our study of intricate multi-dimensional environments, also known as complex landscapes, we explored their categorization based on distinct saddle types, which are comprehensive, connected, and critical points. By applying the principle of analytic continuation, we established the transition between these classifications and demonstrated that pathways to stabilization, either through deepening or amplification, follow standardized paths that are unique and well-defined for each saddle type. Moreover, we calculated the intrinsic densities of these landscapes at standard levels, which will be instrumental in forecasting the evolution of these complex systems as they continue to grow in dimensionality.

To develop optimal methods for identifying symmetric, pure states of quantum systems with limited accessibility, we consider an online scenario where multiple experiments are performed and each measurement result becomes available at various points in time. Several effective methods are developed to identify the state by making the most of newly arrived data at any given moment. Notably, our findings show that a specific strategy based on the QRA estimator is the most optimal approach and should generally be preferred, with further research conducted to compare this result with existing offline identification techniques.

Baryon creation is investigated using a quantized fragmentation model based on QCD strings, with the assumption that baryons consist of connected helical loops and multiple fragments. The model requires that free ends of strings transform into quarks, and baryon formation is explored through quantized string fragmentation. The model's mechanism for baryon production involves a quantized transformation of three quarks from a single string into a baryon, with the requirement that quark creation occurs in sets of three. The model's implementation involves a restriction on lattice field configurations to those that have at least one helix and no point where a helix can split into three separate strings. The model's findings regarding baryon production from a lattice with a specified volume and the corresponding results from numerical calculations are reported. The research indicates that the observed baryon species dependence on temperature is limited, with fluctuations in the helicity of formed baryons increasing in response to temperature. The research also suggests that the quantities measured in experimental calculations on the energy dependence of the helicity of protons and antiprotons are not consistent with a dependence on the temperature or a fragmentation helicity.

In the study of the sun's interior using sound waves, the speed of these waves when moving along the same meridian in opposite directions helps scientists understand the movement of the sun's fluid surface horizontally from the north to the south.  Researchers observed that the longitudinal averages of the speed of these waves change in a predictable pattern over the course of the sun's 11-year activity cycle. 

The goal of the study was to investigate how solar regions with high activity levels affect this predictable pattern in the speed of the sound waves. To do this, the researchers analyzed images from the sun's surface and used these to calculate the movement of the sun's fluid surface around active solar regions. They then simulated the effects of these movements on the speed of the sound waves using a mathematical model and averaged the results to compare them to actual measurements. 

The analysis found that the movement of the sun's fluid surface around solar regions may be contributing to, but does not fully explain, the observed changes in the speed of the sound waves that happen as part of the sun's 11-year activity cycle. 

The research indicates that the movement of the sun's fluid surface on a larger scale surrounding these active solar regions cannot fully account for the observed changes in the speed of the sound waves which are used to study the sun's fluid surface circulation. 

The research is relevant to understanding the sun's behavior and its solar activity and involves the use of the sun's helioseismology.

Researchers from the NANOGrav, Parkes, European, and International Pulsar Timing Array Collaborations have discovered strong evidence suggesting a single source for background noise observed across multiple frequency ranges, which might be linked to the presence of stochastic gravitational waves within the frequency range of 1--100 nHz. They have considered a hypothetical scenario in which these waves originate from early turbulence in the universe brought on by non-helical magnetic fields at the energy scale of the quark confinement phase transition.  To investigate this phenomenon further, researchers used magnetic hydrodynamic simulations to observe the time-evolving dynamics of the magnetic fields and compute the resulting gravitational wave output. They discovered that the simulated gravitational wave spectrum exhibits characteristics of a power-law with an inverse frequency slope and found that the amplitude of this wave spectrum significantly diminishes as the temperature lowers post-quark confinement.  A calculation of the Gravitational Wave Strain that would be detected by the Pulsar Timing Array has shown that the primordial magnetic fields are unable to completely account for the observed residual strain, however they left room for further adjustments within their framework. Moreover, an extensive assessment was conducted to determine whether these cosmological magnetic fields could lead to the detection of Pulsar Timing Array and other gravitational wave detectors detecting a gravitational wave signal in the near future.

Light field technology is currently a focal point of interest for the research community due to its various potential uses. A significant feature of commercial plenoptic cameras, the lenslet array captures spatial and angular light information in a single exposure. However, during image processing, reducing the massive amount of data required to capture light fields proves to be a significant challenge. To overcome this, we have developed a new approach based on machine learning to compress light field images in a practical manner by first estimating angular image disparities from a given light field and then employing these predictions to decrease the size of angular image buffers in compressing light field images. Our Disparity-Aware Model (DAM) has two distinct parts: the angular image disparity prediction network (AIPN) uses a 3D deep convolutional neural network to predict the disparities of angular images, and the angular image reducer network (AIRN) uses these predictions to find a compact representation of angular images. Our model, which includes DAM, significantly outperforms previous methods in terms of compression ratio and PSNR value, with an improvement of over 2 times in compression ratio while maintaining high accuracy. Moreover, we have successfully compressed and compressed the light field captured by a commercial plenoptic camera, achieving superior results compared to other methods.

In cross-lingual information retrieval using vector-based approaches, two general
models exist - interactive and non-interactive models. The former leverages
pre-trained multilingual embeddings, while the latter directly learns its embeddings
from a monolingual dataset. Our study delves into the advantages of these models,
particularly their suitability for specific query translation methods. By exploring
the effect of different query translation techniques on the performance of these
models, we propose a new strategy, leading to an improvement in performance for
specific tasks. Furthermore, we examine the robustness of these models in a real-
world scenario where datasets are unevenly distributed.

The urgent need for comprehensive health and demographic reports has driven an increased focus on geographic analysis, specifically for areas such as newborn and woman coverage.  In many low-income and middle-income nations, detailed statistics are lacking due to the lack of high-quality surveys and censuses.  Therefore, researchers have turned to essential health and demographic estimation methods that incorporate big data sources like mobile phone, GPS tracking, and satellite imagery.  A recent study incorporated various microdata sources, including demographic health surveys, to evaluate the effectiveness of essential health and demographic estimation methods.  This research aimed to not only assess the accuracy of these methods but also to provide guidelines on their implementation.  Findings from a design-based and model-based analysis showed that some model-based approaches yielded results comparable to designed-based estimators.  As a result, researchers are moving towards recommending the use of simple model-based estimators for certain scenarios.  Additionally, incorporating demographic health surveys and population censuses enhanced the accuracy of these model-based estimators.  Furthermore, combining these datasets improved the overall estimation process.  While there are still challenges associated with noise from large data sources, researchers are working to mitigate this issue.

The objective of this study is to propose a semi-classical model representing betting as a coherent information transfer process between two agents through a noisy environment, based on the principles of continuous variable quantum mechanics. This model allows for an initial quantum state at the player's end to become entangled with the bookmaker's state when a bet is placed, with subsequent evolution driven by an entanglement-exchange interaction that depends on the odds set by the bookmaker. This approach is analogous to the Kelly criterion, with the latter defined within a classical mean-field framework. By adopting a semi-classical perspective, we can avoid issues related to quantum measurements that may compromise privacy, in addition to discussing scenarios with discrete frequencies and allowing multiple bookmakers to compete based on the odds offered.

Building on the recently created two-dimensional semiconductor MoSi$_2$N$_4$, our comprehensive study of monolayer MoSi$_2$N$_4$ and similar materials in the Mo-W-Ti and Si-Ge families provides a solid foundation for understanding their functionality. By combining the results of quantum chemical calculations, our analysis shows that a unique alignment of energy bands is likely in all these materials, regardless of their crystal structure. Intriguingly, our neutron spectroscopy analysis reveals that a consistent and strong bond between key atoms exists, regardless of the composition and arrangement of these compounds as evidenced by the fact that purified MoSi$_2$N$_4$ exhibits a large thermal conductivity at room temperature.

The search for $\Sigma^+ \to p \mu^+ \mu^-$ decays utilizing $pp$ collision data collected by LHCb, at centre-of-mass energies of 7 and 8 TeV and an accumulated luminosity of 3 $fb^{-1}$, yields 4 standard deviation excess beyond predicted background counts with no noticeable features found in dimuon invariant mass spectra.

The magnetic field and non-ideal factors are known to be pivotal in the process of stellar formation, but due to simplicity, hydrodynamics models often take precedence over more accurate representations like the alpha-disk model in disk studies. Efforts to bridge the gap between core collapse and mature disk development have been minimal. Our study reexamines the formation of the protoplanetary disk through a core's collapse in turbulence-free, magnetic field-dominated environments with non-ideal factors based on magnetic diffusion factored in. We found the disk formation process to closely resemble traditional models, with the inner disk regions developing quickly, while the outer regions took longer to develop due to decreased efficiency in magnetic diffusion. As a result, the outer disk ends up thinner. By the time one million years have passed, the inner disk edge has developed into the protoplanetary disk, which we found to be similar to the alpha-disk model, especially at larger radii. Our research indicates that the inner region develops faster than the outer region, and key aspects like the outer edge, and inner boundary, as well as mass accretion rates match the alpha-disk model's expectations, except for a slower rate on the outer edge due to magnetic diffusion limitations. Our research now connects our understanding of the early protoplanetary disk and the full protoplanetary disk like never before through detailed process analysis and mass accretion rate calculations.

Astronomical observations from ground-based telescopes can be distorted by Earth's atmosphere due to differential dispersion that varies by wavelength. Observations made from multiple telescopes or spectrographs with narrow bandwidths need to compensate for this effect by correcting their data with atmospheric dispersion models (ADMs) or conducting on-sight measurements. Currently, there are five standardized ADMs in use, each formulated differently with some having been developed from model-fitting methods and others based on measurements from various altitude stations. A study found significant variations in the performance of these models when correcting observations at different altitudes, speeds of travel, and weather conditions. We have, therefore, combined the existing models into a new generation of ADMs that can be accessed online for travel routes all over the globe.

This paper employs a refined hierarchical latent variable model to capture patterns in multi-period time series data, which exhibit dynamics governed by various time-sensitive factors. Traditional stacked RNN-based models lack the capability to accurately capture trends spanning multiple periods and frequently rely on unrealistic assumptions due to the need for predefined feature structures. In contrast, our proposed model incorporates an innovative dependency analysis module, which effectively discovers dependencies between time series variables and their predecessors with minimal theoretical guarantees. By integrating a Bayesian framework, we allow for implicit regularization, yielding accurate outcomes without requiring explicit parameter pruning. Experimental evaluations using synthetic and real-world data sets reveal a substantial improvement in model accuracy and parity with state-of-the-art deep learning and hierarchical approaches.

We establish a connection between continuous logic and Pontryagin duality by finding that the topological group of automorphisms on the dual of a locally compact abelian group is a concrete implementation of a homogeneous structure, which is also universal in a specific sense within the same locale. This realization turns out to be computationally accessible as it corresponds to a Stone space. Furthermore, this concrete representation also manifests as a canonical homomorphism in the context of model theory.

The remarkable effectiveness of deep learning has sparked various concerns regarding ethics, encompassing skewed predictions and data security risks. To address these problems, experts employ fairness metrics, decentralized machine learning methods known as federated learning, or differential privacy. A pioneering study, sponsored by the National Science Foundation's Fairness and Ethics in AI Program, brought leading researchers in machine learning, security, and ethics together. Their fusion of expertise resulted in groundbreaking findings and novel solutions that safeguard against bias and data sensitivity. By applying advanced mathematical and computational techniques, such as cross entropy risk minimization, FedAVG, and differential privacy, to models and gradients, researchers devised new algorithms and evaluated them using real-world applications. Specifically, they utilized images of patients from standard medical datasets, including the Chest X-Ray8, Shope Eye, MIAS datasets, and the CodeX dataset from the University of Maryland's Center for Smart Health and Medical Systems. Moreover, they simulated diverse bias and data security scenarios with varying degrees of personal identifiable information to represent a malicious model trainer's behavior. A comparative assessment was conducted on the same dataset with the same model, but when training the model using the dataset on the client, the model trainer has no information. These experiments showed that taking PDI when training the model on the client results in zero personal identifiable information. A differential privacy algorithm was applied to the training process by the model trainer which showed that with higher sensitivity (epsilon) values, accuracy decreases slightly for fair models, but security exponentially

We propose a supersymmetric expansion of a basic $U(1)_X$ model with a new and innovative framework by introducing a $Z_2$ symmetry, which successfully incorporates a $B-L$ breaking scale in a hidden manner, and thus achieves a highly distinctive signature at the LHC and a novel and promising dark matter candidate that naturally satisfies current experimental limits and future prospective studies.

We investigate a smart reflecting surface-aided wireless-powered communication network where a multi-antenna energy transmitter broadcasts an exclusive energy signal to a powered transmitter that then communicates with its destination over a selected path. The energy transmitter's energy efficiency is constrained due to interference caused by other channels. To optimize this setup, we employ a neural network to automatically learn and adjust an optimal non-convex energy optimization problem. The resulting problem is then solved using a gradient descent algorithm when the neural network is trained. Our simulation results demonstrate a substantial increase of up to 35% in throughput compared to a network without the incorporated smart reflecting surface. Moreover, the neural network offers a suitable alternative when dealing with complex optimization problems of IRS-assisted wireless-powered communication networks.

For the first time, researchers used total absorption gamma spectroscopy to measure the Gamow-Teller strength distribution in $^{186}$Hg decaying into $^{186}$Au and compared it to theoretical QRPA calculations employing the SLy4 Skyrme force. The measured strength distribution, alongside the nuclei's half-lives, is best explained by incorporating a combination of proton and neutron transitions. We analyzed various factors contributing to the quasiparticle unfolding procedure and calculated the total strength for both the feedout and foldout processes. The experimental and theoretical strength distributions for both nuclei are in good agreement for energies up to around 11 MeV, indicating that the theoretical model accurately captures shape fluctuations in heavy, neutron-deficient nuclei. For the $^{186}$Hg sample with a 93$\pm$11 s half-life, theoretical QRPA calculations support a 54$\pm$11 s half-life, while the $^{190}$Hg isotope with a 9.3$\pm$0.4 ms half-life remains in line with 2019 values. Furthermore, the data indicate that the isotopic distribution in the $z$-quasiparticle band is reduced in $^{186}$Hg and $^{190}$Hg, while the $|\Delta N|-|{\Delta iz}|$ quasiparticle band exhibits increased fragmentation.

We explore the intersection of dark matter and leptogenesis within a unified framework based on the $U(1)$ extension of the Standard Model. This involves a dark sector with its own neutral current, comprising a $5$-dose leptonic Majorana mass and a sterile neutrino as a dark matter candidate. We find that the dark matter mass is tied to the heavy neutrino mass, which in turn, determines the relic density and direct detection constraints. Furthermore, our analysis reveals a dark matter density in agreement with the Planck observation, while simultaneously levelling off strong constraints from XENON100 and X-FACTORY experiments. Additionally, our framework generates a small neutrino mass in accordance with the neutrino mass scaling $\Delta m_{11}^2$, consistent with a low-scale right-handed neutrino content, and consistent with a large leptogenesis common denominator. Consequently, our findings illustrate the complexity of reconciling signatures of both dark matter and leptogenesis within a unified framework based on the Standard Model.

The vast amounts of data collected by sensors could significantly enhance our ability to control complex systems, however due to privacy concerns and logistical difficulties collecting data from physical systems it is often limited. To address this issue, researchers have been exploring strategies that enable control system design with a single trial on complex, multi-dimensional systems that adapt to unknown dynamics. Building on the success of prior work by Coulson et al. that utilized baseline information for single-trial control of complex systems, this study tackles the challenge of controlling multi-dimensional systems that undergo continuous dynamics shifts and has results applied to diverse domains such as physics and biology. Our data-driven approach for single-trial control also considers the practical issue of generalizing across different conditions in dynamic systems and applies this to diverse domains. Furthermore, baseline information is not always available, and in such cases, machine learning can suggest alternative strategies, and we demonstrate this in controlling multiple flight robots with different physical characteristics through the development of a general framework.

The Toda conformal field theory based on $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ as the underlying Lie algebra contains a field, $e^{q(x)}$, where $q(x)$ is a non-linear function. This theory has a unique property due to the presence of a'self-duality' field, $\delta M(x)$, which when applied to the field $e^{q(x)}$, yields a first derivative. This unusual property gives rise to a set of novel Ward identities distinct from those in minimal conformal field theories. These ward identities provide the basis for the'vertex operator algebras' that are used to construct the theory as well as the 'conformal Toda systems' of equations that describe the theory's dynamics. Moreover, the presence of the 'duality field' enables the development of an exact 'quantum background' for the theory. This means that the theory can be represented using a constant two-form $B$ without affecting its dynamics.

Despite significant advancements in decreasing the diversity within synthetic images, generating diverse realistic images remains a challenging task.
